subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept a custom cooperative replacement for Node glob resolution and yield between agent-bootstrap hook handlers to protect embedded-run event-loop responsiveness?
rationale: Tests and the supplied benchmark support the intended improvement, but selecting the long-term glob-parity and hook-scheduling contract is an owner-level runtime decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Approve the cooperative runtime policy
options.body: Accept the bounded scheduling tradeoff after owners confirm that preserving tested Node-glob compatibility is sufficient for configured bootstrap files.

options.title: Narrow to async root reads and diagnostics
options.body: Keep the lower-risk asynchronous file-read and timing work, but defer custom traversal and hook scheduling until an owner-designed runtime policy exists.

options.title: Pause for a platform-parity design
options.body: Hold this PR if OpenClaw requires a stronger cross-platform glob and handler-ordering contract before replacing the platform implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve the cooperative runtime policy
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded scheduling tradeoff after owners confirm that preserving tested Node-glob compatibility is sufficient for configured bootstrap files.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question is a runtime-direction decision, and this person was explicitly engaged on the PR discussion.
